ai_overview:
Tsukiji Outer Market offers a vibrant, historic street-food experience, while Toyosu Fish Market is a modern, high-tech wholesale facility famous for the early-morning tuna auctions. 
Reddit
·r/JapanTravel
 +3
Tsukiji Outer Market
Vibe: Bustling, historic open-air market with a dense maze of narrow alleyways and old-school energy. 
Instagram
·Jerry Archer
 +1
Best For: Street food (tamagoyaki, seafood skewers, onigiri), casual counter sushi, and shopping for kitchen tools like Japanese knives. 
Seaside with Emily
 +2
Logistics: Free entry, no reservations needed, open early morning through early afternoon (best to arrive by 8:00 AM). Closed on Sundays and select Wednesdays. 
Tanuki Tabi Travel
 +1
Access: Tsukiji Station (Hibiya Line) or Tsukijishijo Station (Oedo Line). 
Seaside with Emily
Toyosu Fish Market
Vibe: Clean, sterile, airport-terminal-style commercial facility located on a man-made island. 
YouTube
·welcometojapan
 +2
Best For: Watching the famous bluefin tuna auctions and visiting high-end sushi and seafood restaurants. 
MICHELIN Guide
 +2
Logistics: Open 5:00 AM to 5:00 PM (closed Sundays, most Wednesdays, and holidays). Viewing the tuna auction from the lower observation deck requires winning an online advance lottery (or watching for free from upper public windows/galleries). 
Tokyo Cheapo
 +1
Access: Shijo-mae Station (Yurikamome Line). 
www.hotandchilli.com
 +1
Which Should You Choose?
Choose Tsukiji if you want to graze on street food, soak in traditional market culture, and eat casual sushi without planning ahead.
Choose Toyosu if you want to see the industrial-scale tuna auction or experience modern Japanese seafood distribution.
Do Both: Many visitors arrive early at Toyosu for the auction, then head straight to Tsukiji for breakfast. 
Tanuki Tabi Travel
 +2
